method.label: Magnitudes and a forced final factor

annotationRationale: Complex magnitudes force the eight-and-four split. Complex multiplication shows that the fourth factor from B has exactly one successful value. Combinations select the positions, and equally likely ordered outcomes give the probability.
sourceMethod: Followed the official modulus split and unique completion by the last factor from B. Expressed the probability as an equivalent count of ordered selections and used multiples of i to justify the unique completion.

review.mathCheck: Independently, the modulus condition is 2^(3k/2−12)=1, forcing eight A-factors and four B-factors. Fixing the A-factors and three B-factors leaves exactly one successful fourth B-value. Thus the probability is C(12,4)·2^8·4^3/6^12=220/59049, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Matches official solution 25 on attached page 12: separate by modulus, then force the final B-factor. The independently worded adaptation supplies a valid algebraic explanation of the four possible products and an equivalent counting argument.
review.annotationCheck: The four assessed nodes describe the substantive method; h104 appropriately supports the power calculations. Neither polar form nor binomial-distribution knowledge is required.
